subject: SLA amendment request: uptime baseline & credit activation (OpsDeck)
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara@opsdeck.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: SLA amendment request: uptime baseline & credit activation (OpsDeck)

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput improvements look promising. OpsDeck legal and I reviewed Redwood's standard SLA and we have a couple of asks before we can move to signature: 

1) Uptime baseline: for our production inference endpoints in us-west we need a baseline of 99.5% (monthly) instead of the 99.9% in the template. This is because our workload is heavily batched and has predictable maintenance windows.

2) Credit activation: we want a clear monthly activation threshold and calculation. Our request: if monthly uptime falls below 99.5%, the customer credit is equal to X% of that month's invoice where X = min( (99.5 - observed_uptime) / 0.5 * 50%, 100% ). In plain terms: a linear band where a 0.5% shortfall maps to a 50% credit, capped at 100% of that month.

3) Cap / escrow: we expect a per-month cap of 100% of that month’s invoice but would like to discuss a maximum 2x annual cap for extreme cases.

I've attached OpsDeck_reqs_v1.pdf with a short rationale and our security contact information. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the 99.5% baseline for this account as an SLATemplate exception, and if the credit formula above is compatible with Redwood's remediation and invoicing processes?

We'd like to close the commercial terms this week and route the paper to legal. If it helps, OpsDeck legal (cc'd separately) can redline in parallel.

Thanks,
Sara Li
Head of Platform Ops, OpsDeck
Sara Li
opsdeck.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request: uptime baseline & credit activation (OpsDeck)

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and for the doc. Looping in Laura (commercial counsel) and Ben (account lead) so we can move quickly.

A few quick responses and a Redwood-first pass at redlines:

- Baseline: Redwood's hosted default for production endpoints is 99.9% monthly. We can evaluate a 99.5% baseline for OpsDeck as an exception tied specifically to your batched inference workloads and a scoped list of endpoints. In practice we'd like to limit the exception to endpoints using the "batching" routing policy — this keeps the broader product SLA intact.

- Credit activation / formula: Your linear band is reasonable, but our billing system expects credits expressed as a percentage of the monthly invoice with a clear floor. Proposed Redwood-friendly wording: "If monthly uptime < 99.5% for scoped endpoints, customer will receive a service credit calculated as (99.5% - observed_uptime) / 0.5 * 50% of that month's invoice for the scoped service, capped at 100% for that month." This matches your intent but uses language we can operationalize.

- Cap / escrow: We typically cap per-month credits at 100% of that month's billing for the service in scope. A 2x annual cap is plausible but needs executive sign-off — can you share the justification and the expected monthly spend so we can run the numbers?

I've attached an initial redline (redwood_sla_redline.docx) with the scoped-endpoint language, an explicit carveout for batched routing policy, and a proposed monitoring/measurement paragraph (source of truth = Redwood's monthly availability report + customer-provided telemetry).

Next steps I suggest:
- Ben, can you confirm commercial impact and whether OpsDeck's expected monthly commit supports a 2x annual cap discussion?
- Laura, please advise on whether the proposed wording is acceptable to legal or if OpsDeck legal should redline directly.

Sara — if you're available this afternoon I can jump on a 30-min call to walk the redlines.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_sla_redline.docx

Sara / Team — quick commercial counter-proposal to accelerate:

1) We agree to the scoped 99.5% baseline for batched endpoints.
2) Service credit calculation — we accept Redwood's operational wording as Mark outlined.
3) Credit cap — Redwood can accept a per-month cap of 100% of that month’s scoped service invoice. For the annual cap, we can offer a negotiated protective cap up to 2x the monthly invoice aggregated across the 12 months (i.e., an emergency protection bucket) but only with a minimum 12-month committed spend of $60k. If OpsDeck can commit to that minimum, we will include the 2x annual cap in the SOW.

I've attached a short proposed-credit-matrix.csv that maps observed uptime bands to percent credit to make the calculation explicit for legal.

If that looks good we can generate a DocuSign package with the SLA amendment + SOW. Would OpsDeck be comfortable with a short alignment call tomorrow to finalize the minimum commit?

Thanks,
